title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Broadcast Test Card. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Broadcast Test Card
options.lineage: 1967-80 transmitted test cards and calibration slides
options.thesis: A transmitted calibration image, which is what a complex signal looks like when somebody has already made it legible.
options.viewport: The FM tab. An 88px calibration strip across the top holds the live scope trace and the limiter's gain reduction as bar segments; below it the six operator columns, envelope section and mod matrix sit on phosphor ground, with the sidebar as a tinted rail.
options.risk: Test cards are a strong, dated graphic. If the bars are decorative rather than carrying state, it reads as a novelty wallpaper.

raised.raise: The calibration strip re-solves continuously: scope trace, bar segments and operator columns all respond live to one held note, so the screen proves it is an instrument before you touch it.
Every operator cell is a live thumbnail in a packed grid at full density, not six wide panels with air between them.
The modulation spine is the one moving part: a single rail between the operator grid and the mod matrix carrying the routing keys, and the only thing that relocates.
Every value sits directly beside the control that produces it, paired rather than listed, so a reading is never separated from its cause.
The construction grid is visible as the armature: the operator matrix and the mod matrix share one measurable cell, drawn rather than implied.

options.label: The Folded Schematic
options.lineage: fold-out service-manual schematics and drafting standards
options.thesis: The document that explains the machine, which is the whole promise of the product.
options.viewport: The FM tab as a schematic sheet: operators as labelled blocks, the routing matrix as the drawn signal path, modulation sources annotated in the margin.
options.risk: It is the direction most runs in this category land on: engineering-blue as a safe skin.

options.label: The Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: The object where a personal recording becomes something you keep.
options.viewport: Patches as an inked tracklist, running times right-aligned, sides as hard halves.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins audience identification outright: this is exactly the culture the user is in. It loses on product clarity, because the screen becomes a tracklist rather than a working instrument.
options.risk: Deeply nostalgic, and it makes the synth look like a thing you listen to rather than play.

options.label: The Variable Specimen
options.thesis: One axis, dragged, remaps an entire field of glyphs live.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience is type people, and a specimen is not a working instrument. Declined on both axes.
options.kept: Live continuous remapping, one drag re-solving the whole field with no intermediate state.

options.label: The Event Catalog
options.thesis: Eight hundred thumbnails on one sheet, every one the size of a stamp, each keyed to a place.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the screen becomes a catalogue to browse, not an instrument to play. Declined on both axes.
options.kept: Total density courage: a whole-page live grid where every cell carries real content at postage-stamp size.

options.label: The Centre Rail
options.thesis: Two dense columns twinned around a hairline rail of keys, everything drawn at one device pixel.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it reads as a printed book page, and its apparatus marks are not affordances a player already knows. Declined on both axes.
options.kept: The one moving part: a single centre rail carries every key and detent, and nothing else in the layout relocates.

options.label: The Monochrome Claim
options.thesis: A fine neutral scale, one accent used four times, every claim paired with its proof.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is a marketing page, and a grey screen with one accent is the category default without the category's polish. Declined on both axes.
options.kept: Claim and proof in strict adjacency: a reading never appears apart from the control that produced it.

options.label: The Visible Armature
options.thesis: Letterforms assembled cell by cell on a construction grid that stays visible as the design.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a specimen poster is not a working instrument, and the grid becomes ornament the moment nothing is measured by it. Declined on both axes.
options.kept: The grid as literal, drawn armature rather than an implied one.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a synth plugin ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark grey panel, top tab bar, operator columns of identical knobs, one blue accent on the selected state.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
